conviction_note: Consensus Q1 FY27 revenue of $29.6M implies only +3.5% sequential off Q4's $28.64M, against +12.8% and +27% in the company's two prior Q4-to-Q1 transitions, and an independent FDA MDR-volume proxy is up 58% sequentially over the same fiscal quarter; I size the upside small (+2.7) rather than large because KMTS beat Q4 revenue by 8% and raised the FY guide above street and the stock still only moved +1.8%, so the revenue-beat reaction function on this name is visibly damped.

findings.finding: Consensus for tonight ($29.6M revenue) implies only +3.5% sequential growth off Q4 FY26's $28.64M, whereas Kestra's two prior fiscal-Q4-to-Q1 transitions were +27% ($10.1M to $12.8M) and +12.8% ($17.23M to $19.37M), and its worst-ever within-year sequential was +8.8% — at +8.8% Q1 prints ~$31.1M and at last year's +12.8% it prints ~$32.3M; the same set of press releases shows FY26 guidance walked $85M (initial, 15 Jul 2025) to $88M to $91M to $93M to an actual $95.1M, i.e. the initial guide was beaten by 11.9% with a raise at all four quarters, and the FY27 initial guide of $137M (+44%) was set off an exiting +66% quarter using the identical framing.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus itself is the evidence that it is not priced: five estimates have anchored on the fiscal-year guidance rate (+44%) rather than on the company's own quarterly sequential pattern, producing a Q1 number that requires the weakest quarter-on-quarter step in KMTS's public history and a one-quarter deceleration from +66% to +52.6% y/y. If the sequential pattern were in the price, the Q1 consensus would sit near $31M and the stock would not have de-rated 15.9% over 20 sessions with zero company-specific news on the tape (the only KMTS releases since 31 Aug are two personnel announcements and the earnings-date notice). The counterweight, which is why I size this small, is that the Q4 print already delivered an 8% revenue beat plus an above-street FY27 guide ($137M vs $133M consensus) for only +1.8%.
findings.independence: The quarterly revenue series and the guidance walk come from the same cluster of Kestra press releases, so I file them as ONE finding rather than two - they are one document set and must count once. Separate corroboration of the quarterly actuals and the FY27-guide-above-consensus point comes from MarketBeat's earnings history page: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/KMTS/earnings/ ; the FY26 quarterly prints are at https://investors.kestramedical.com/news-releases/news-release-details/kestra-medical-technologies-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-2026 (2025-09-11, $19.4M), https://www.stocktitan.net/news/KMTS/kestra-medical-technologies-reports-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-ty601w7mk461.html (2026-03-17, $24.6M) and https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/14/3327235/0/en/Kestra-Medical-Technologies-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results.html (2026-07-14, $28.6M); the $85M initial FY26 guide is on the company's 2025-07-15 release page https://investors.kestramedical.com/news-releases/news-release-details/kestra-medical-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal (snippet_only - the page returned 503 on direct fetch).

findings.finding: openFDA device adverse-event (MDR) filings naming KESTRA as manufacturer run 43 / 56 / 50 for May / June / July 2026 = 149 for Kestra's fiscal Q1 FY2027, against 38 / 30 / 26 = 94 for fiscal Q4 FY2026 (Feb-Apr 2026), a +58% sequential rise, with August 2026 at 72 the single highest month in the series - an installed-base proxy that is independent of anything the company has said and that points the opposite way to the +3.5% sequential revenue consensus.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-14 (API queried today; series runs Feb 2022 - Aug 2026)
findings.why_not_priced: No aggregator, sell-side preview or wire item converts MAUDE report counts into a patients-on-service proxy for this name; if it were being read, the Q1 consensus would not sit at the weakest sequential in company history while the field-event count rose 58% over the same three months. What would visibly differ: a preview note or a Zacks/Quiver blurb quoting MDR volume, or a Q1 consensus revised up in the weeks after the July and August MDR months landed.
findings.independence: Fully independent of the company's own filings and of finding 1 - it is an FDA database, not a Kestra document. IMPORTANT CAVEAT that cuts my size: Kestra made a 296-report batch filing in November 2025 covering a gap in which Apr-Sep 2025 all show zero, so reporting practice demonstrably changed and a year-on-year comparison is unusable; only the Dec-2025-onward cadence looks regular, and part of the level rise could still be compliance clean-up rather than volume. Corroborating direction from a different source: Kestra's Greenhouse board today carries ~50 open 1099 'Patient Specialist' (device-fitter) requisitions nationwide against only 3 open Territory Manager roles - https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/kestramedicaltechnologiesinc

findings.finding: Asahi Kasei told its 31 July 2026 earnings call that ZOLL's LifeVest WCD grew in the low-10% range in the US and just under 15% in Europe in April-June 2026 - a category read-across published seventeen days after Kestra last spoke (14 July), showing the US WCD market expanding rather than contracting even as the incumbent rolled out its fifth-generation device and a new garment.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody covering a $1.4bn US small-cap reads a Japanese chemical conglomerate's quarterly segment call, and Asahi Kasei does not break LifeVest out in any English release that reaches US wires. If it were priced, at least one KMTS preview would reference incumbent WCD growth as the category anchor; none does. Small size because it is confirmatory of the existing bull framing rather than new in direction - it says the market is growing, which is what Kestra already claims.
findings.independence: Independent of findings 1 and 2 (third-party issuer disclosure). Same-direction corroboration that the incumbent is investing behind a growing category rather than harvesting it: https://www.asahi-kasei.com/news/2026/e260108-2 (2026-01-08, US launch of next-generation LifeVest).

baseline_tension: My net positive agrees with the free control (-run_up_20d_pct would also rank this name long after a 15.9% 20-day de-rating on no news), which makes it less differentiated than I would like, and it cuts against the company's own recent reaction function - an 8% revenue beat plus an above-consensus FY27 guide bought only +1.8% in July and a beat-and-raise bought -7.4% in March, with EPS missed in three of the last four quarters - which is exactly why I have sized a 5-9% revenue beat at under half the baseline's 5.77% historical median move rather than at or above it.
